column3: Summary
column4: Description

column3: E1 Accounts, roles and financial privacy
column4: Individual accounts, four roles (dentist, informaticienne, receptionist, assistant) and revenue totals visible to the dentist only. Traces to C1 (FR-01 to FR-06, NFR-08, BR-06).

column3: E2 Patient record and treatment follow-up
column4: Patient record with latest session first, prominent dates, dated progress notes, treatment decision and treatment catalog. Traces to C2 (FR-07 to FR-12).

column3: E3 Appointments and emergencies
column4: Appointment dates set by the dentist, no double-booking, emergency insertion, day list. Traces to C3, C4 (FR-13 to FR-19).

column3: E4 Payments and balances
column4: Cash instalments, price, remaining balance, receptionist balance view. Traces to C5 (FR-20 to FR-24).

column3: E5 Medical alerts
column4: Anamnese for at-risk patients and a visible alert on the record. Traces to C6 (FR-25 to FR-27).

column3: E6 New-patient share and dentist indicators
column4: New/existing flag, 40% target, patients per day, session duration, no-show rate. Traces to C7, C10 (FR-28, FR-29, FR-37 to FR-40).

column3: E7 Waiting queue and Oralia link
column4: Clinic-side queue management and the minimal data sent for the Oralia mobile app. Traces to C8, C9 (FR-30 to FR-36, NFR-09).

column3: E8 Reliability, backup and performance
column4: Power-cut safety, daily backup, two PCs sharing data on the LAN, speed. Traces to NFR-01, 02, 04 to 07.

column3: Record the next appointment on the dentist's date
column4:
As a receptionist, I want to enter the next appointment date that the dentist gives me, so that the patient's treatment continues as he decided.

Acceptance criteria:
- Appointment stores surname, first name, telephone and treatment progress
- The date is typed by the receptionist; the system never suggests a date
- Booking works for phone and on-site requests

Traceability: FR-13, FR-14, FR-19
Priority (MoSCoW): Must | Release: 1
Assumption: story text and criteria are a draft, to be confirmed with the dentist.

column3: Prevent double-booking
column4:
As a receptionist, I want the system to refuse a slot that is already taken, so that two patients are never booked at the same time.

Acceptance criteria:
- A taken slot is refused with a clear French message
- An emergency insertion is the only allowed exception (see emergency story)

Traceability: FR-15, BR-02
Priority (MoSCoW): Must | Release: 1
Assumption: story text and criteria are a draft, to be confirmed with the dentist.

column3: Insert an emergency patient in one action
column4:
As a receptionist, I want to insert an emergency patient into today's list in one action, so that the dentist can take the emergency without breaking the schedule.

Acceptance criteria:
- One action adds the patient to the current day
- Other appointments of the day are kept
- The emergency is marked as such in the day list

Traceability: FR-16, BR-02
Priority (MoSCoW): Must | Release: 1
Assumption: story text and criteria are a draft, to be confirmed with the dentist.

column3: Record a cash payment
column4:
As a receptionist, I want to record a cash instalment with an optional code note (for example V1 = 1,000 DA), so that every payment is kept.

Acceptance criteria:
- Payment stores amount, date, method (cash by default) and optional code note
- Payment is saved immediately
- Presets or a fast entry reduce typing

Traceability: FR-21, BR-04
Priority (MoSCoW): Must | Release: 1
Assumption: story text and criteria are a draft, to be confirmed with the dentist.

column3: Set the treatment price and see the remaining balance
column4:
As the dentist, I want each treatment to have a price and a remaining balance, so that I know what a patient still owes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Balance = price minus the sum of payments
- Example: price 40,000 DA, paid 20,000 + 4,000, balance 16,000 DA
- Balance updates after each payment

Traceability: FR-20, FR-22, BR-05
Priority (MoSCoW): Must | Release: 1
Assumption: story text and criteria are a draft, to be confirmed with the dentist.

column3: View an individual patient's balance
column4:
As a receptionist, I want to see one patient's balance, so that I can tell him what remains to pay, without seeing the clinic's totals.

Acceptance criteria:
- Receptionist sees the balance of one patient
- Receptionist cannot open any revenue total

Traceability: FR-23
Priority (MoSCoW): Must | Release: 1
Assumption: story text and criteria are a draft, to be confirmed with the dentist.

column3: Keep revenue totals private to the dentist
column4:
As the dentist, I want only my account to see daily and monthly revenue totals, so that my financial data stays private.

Acceptance criteria:
- Informaticienne and receptionist cannot open any total in the interface
- A direct server or database query from those roles is refused

Traceability: FR-05, NFR-08, BR-06
Priority (MoSCoW): Must | Release: 1
Assumption: story text and criteria are a draft, to be confirmed with the dentist.

column3: Log in with an individual account
column4:
As a staff member, I want to log in with my own account, so that my actions are traceable and my screens match my role.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each staff member has a personal login
- Unauthenticated users cannot open any screen

Traceability: FR-01

Assumption: story text and criteria are a draft, to be confirmed with the dentist.

column3: Role-based access to screens and actions
column4:
As the dentist, I want the four roles to have different rights, so that each nurse sees and edits only what her work requires.

Acceptance criteria:
- Four roles exist: dentist, informaticienne, receptionist, assistant
- Informaticienne writes patients, notes, anamnese, treatment plans and sessions
- Receptionist handles queue, appointments and payment entry

column3: Register a patient

Acceptance criteria:
